events.type: sector move (AI-spending doubts; rates and oil)
events.summary: Thursday's chip sell-off: in the morning, rising Treasury yields and oil weighed on growth stocks (SOXX -2% by 10:05 ET); later a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue was $20 billion lower than previously estimated hit AI-linked stocks. The SOX index fell as much as 4% intraday; Nasdaq -1.25% to 27,193.34, S&P 500 -0.47% to 7,765.36, Dow +0.1%. Brent about $104 a barrel, 10-year yield 5.23%. SMH fell -2.84% (computed). ASML closed -1.95% at $1,769.79, near its day low of $1,763.23, after trading as high as $1,842.53 (+2.08%) earlier.
events.why_it_matters: ASML's customers buy machines because they expect AI chip demand to keep growing; news that casts doubt on whether AI companies earn enough to keep spending hits equipment stocks first. This, not ASML news, explains most of Thursday's fall (industry part -2.50 of -1.95).

events.summary: Reuters reported that engineers from ASML and its optics partner Carl Zeiss published a peer-reviewed paper (Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning, Materials, and Metrology, vol. 25 issue 4, October 2026: 'Hyper-NA: a system with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75') describing 'Hyper NA', a possible successor to High-NA EUV that 'could be ready in about 10 years' and print features 'as small as 5 nanometers, more than a third smaller' than High NA. ASML's current light source 'can be reused as is'; the machine would be 'barely larger than High NA tools'. ASML 'has begun developing but has not committed to producing' it; ASML had no immediate comment. Same Reuters piece: Intel uses High NA in production; Samsung and SK Hynix said last month they would follow in 2028, TSMC in 2030. ASML traded +1.3% at $1,828.35 around 11:05 ET (GuruFocus) before the sector sell-off.
events.why_it_matters: Supports Thesis 1 (the monopoly): it shows a credible technology path beyond today's best machine, reusing parts only ASML and Zeiss make, which keeps rivals further behind. It adds no revenue for roughly a decade and ASML has not committed to building it.
events.note: The DOI resolves to the SPIE Digital Library page for the paper (title confirmed from the URL); the paper text itself could not be loaded.

events.summary: Samsung Electronics, one of ASML's largest customers, guided Q3 2026 consolidated operating profit of approximately KRW 107.40 trillion and sales of approximately KRW 195 trillion (preliminary, K-IFRS). Korea JoongAng Daily: operating profit +782.5% year on year, above the FnGuide consensus of KRW 106 trillion; sales below the KRW 200.3 trillion forecast. First Korean company above KRW 100 trillion in a quarter; memory (HBM and DRAM) the main driver. No capital-spending figures were given; division detail comes with full results later in October. Released 8 Oct Korea time, i.e. after Wednesday's US close and before Thursday's US open (exact release time not verified).
events.why_it_matters: A customer earning record profits from memory has the cash and the reason to keep buying machines (Thesis 2, pillar 4), and Samsung plans High-NA EUV from 2028. But profit is not spending: no capex number yet, so trigger 5 cannot be tested until Samsung's full results. No source tied ASML's move to it; ASML opened -0.73% Thursday.

why_chain.text: ASML fell -1.95% on Thursday to $1,769.79 and rose +0.60% on Friday to $1,780.34: -1.36% over two days, while the chip fund SMH fell -3.47% and the S&P 500 fund SPY rose +0.17% (computed).

The chip sector explains the fall; ASML itself did better than its sector. Two-day split: market +0.14, industry -3.78, company +2.28 (z 1.02, normal size). Thursday: -0.33 / -2.50 / +0.88; Friday: +0.47 / -1.30 / +1.42.

Thursday's chip sell-off had two published causes: higher Treasury yields and oil in the morning (inflation worries hit growth stocks), then a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue was $20 billion lower than previously estimated, which cast doubt on AI spending; the SOX index fell as much as 4%.

ASML had its own good news that morning (Reuters on the ASML-Zeiss 'Hyper NA' paper, published before the US open); it traded +1.3% around 11:05 ET and reached +2.08% at the day high before reversing almost 4% to close near the low with the sector.

The positive company part (+0.88 Thursday, +1.42 Friday) is consistent with ASML-specific support from the Hyper NA report and from its customers' strong numbers (Samsung record profit; TSMC September sales +54.6%), but no source states that link.

Friday: oil eased and Bloomberg reported OpenAI expects at least $70 billion annualized revenue by year-end, so tech rebounded at the open (ASML +2.79% at the open); chip stocks then faded (SMH -0.65%) and ASML gave back most of its gain. No published reason for the chip fade was found.

Basic driver: investors are re-pricing how long AI spending lasts, and they react to evidence on whether AI companies such as OpenAI earn enough to keep paying for chips. That expectation feeds directly into how many machines chipmakers will order from ASML.

products.name: Hyper NA EUV (research concept, not a product)
products.what_it_is: A possible future generation of ASML's chip-printing machine that would use a wider lens opening (numerical aperture of at least 0.75, versus 0.55 for today's High NA) to print even smaller circuit features.
products.analogy: Like a camera with a bigger lens that can capture finer detail: same flash (the light source) as before, but a wider aperture so it can draw sharper, tinier lines.
products.buyers: Would be the makers of the most advanced chips (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix); none has ordered it, because it does not exist yet.
products.how_it_works: EUV light bounces off ultra-precise Zeiss mirrors that focus a circuit pattern onto a silicon wafer. A larger numerical aperture lets the optics gather light at wider angles, which sharpens the image. The paper says Hyper NA could print features as small as 5 nanometers, reuse ASML's current light source 'as is', and be 'barely larger' than High NA (Reuters).
products.price: not disclosed (no price for High NA or Hyper NA in the Reuters report)
products.sales: None: ASML 'has begun developing but has not committed to producing' it (Reuters). Labelled proxy: ASML recognised 48 EUV systems in 2025, of which 4 were the current High NA (EXE) model and 44 the standard NXE model.
products.sales_source: https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/asml-zeiss-say-next-generation-chipmaking-technology-may-be-ready-10-years (Reuters, 2026-10-08); units from ASML 20-F FY2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/937966/000162828026011378/asml-20251231.htm) as summarised in reports/deep-dives/ASML-2026-10-04.md
products.stage: Research and early development; peer-reviewed design paper published October 2026; 'could be ready in about 10 years'.
products.size_for_company: Zero revenue for roughly a decade. Its value today is strategic: it extends the monopoly runway beyond High NA, whose customer adoption is itself only starting (Intel now; Samsung and SK Hynix 2028; TSMC 2030, per Reuters).
products.competition: No company outside ASML makes EUV machines today (ASML 20-F FY2025). Zeiss is ASML's exclusive optics partner; ASML owns 24.9% of Carl Zeiss SMT (20-F, per deep dive).
products.why_investors_care: Shows the technology road does not end with High NA, which supports the view that ASML's lead lasts into the late 2030s. The cost is more R&D years before any sales.
products.watch_next: Any mention of Hyper NA or a commitment decision on the 10-14 call or at the Capital Markets Day on 2027-06-10.

products.name: Spare parts and components for installed EUV/DUV machines (reported 10% price rise, unconfirmed)
products.what_it_is: Replacement and repair parts (optical systems, light sources, precision drive units) that keep chipmakers' ASML machines running; part of what ASML calls Installed Base Management (service and upgrades).
products.analogy: Like a printer maker that also sells the ink and the repair kits: every machine sold keeps generating parts orders for years.
products.buyers: Every chipmaker that owns ASML machines; the report names Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
products.how_it_works: Machines wear out consumable parts and need repairs; only ASML (with suppliers such as Zeiss) can supply certified parts, so it sets prices under service contracts and purchase agreements.
products.price: not disclosed; reported increase of 10% from January 2027 (tier 3, unconfirmed)
products.sales: Parts sales not disclosed separately. Labelled proxy: Installed Base Management sales (service plus field options) were EUR 2,762m in Q2 2026 and EUR 8,193.0m in 2025 (25.1% of sales); Q3 2026 guided at about EUR 2.9bn.
products.sales_source: ASML Q2 2026 results 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/937966/000162828026048235/pressreleasefinancialresul.htm); 20-F FY2025; Q3 IBM guide of about EUR 2.9bn from the Q2 investor presentation as recorded in data/research/2026-10-07/ASML.json
products.stage: Shipping (existing business); the price rise is reported for January 2027.
products.size_for_company: Not computable without the parts share of IBM. For scale only: if 10% were applied to the whole EUR 8.2bn 2025 IBM base it would be about EUR 0.8bn a year (computed upper bound, not a forecast; the report covers only parts and only two customers).
products.competition: Essentially none for genuine ASML parts at the leading edge; customers' leverage is negotiation (TSMC reportedly resisted earlier price-rise proposals, Bloomberg/The Information 2026-07-15).
products.why_investors_care: Price rises that customers accept are the clearest proof of pricing power (Thesis 1) and lift the steady service income (Thesis 3).
products.watch_next: Whether ASML confirms or comments on pricing on 2026-10-14; gross margin vs the 55-57% Q3 guide; any TSMC comment on 10-15.
